title: Protocol for arrayed gRNA screening by base editors in mammalian cell lines using lentiviral system
protocol: Digest the lentiviral vector (Addgene #57822) using the BsmB1 enzyme.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 55°C for 3 hours.
Perform gel electrophoresis of the digested product on a 0.8% agarose gel for at least 90 minutes.
Load the undigested plasmid in an adjacent well as a control for digestion.
Carefully excise the desired digested backbone (∼8000 bp) using a clean blade.
Purify the excised DNA using the Zymo gel purification Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute the purified product in 25 μL of nuclease-free water.
Adjust the concentration of the purified product to 50 ng/μL.
Reconstitute the lyophilized forward and reverse oligos to 100 pm concentration.
Set up the annealing reaction in a PCR tube.
Take 1 μL of annealed product and dilute it (1:200) using sterile water.
Store at 4°C until use.
Prepare LB Agar plate with ampicillin (100 μg/mL).
Thaw 50 μL of DH10B competent cells on ice.
Add 6 μL of ligated product to the cells and mix by flicking the tubes.
Keep on ice for 30 min.
Set up water bath at 42°C.
Give heat shock for 45 s at 42°C.
Rapidly transfer to an ice bath and incubate for 5 min.
Plate the whole volume on LB Ampicillin plate.
Incubate at 37°C for 12–14 h.
Check the control plate and ensure that there are no colonies.
Prepare LB broth (3 mL for each gRNA).
Arrange 2 mL tubes containing one mL of LB broth (with ampicillin), 3 tubes for each gRNA.
Pick and inoculate 3 isolated colonies into this LB broth from the plate.
Keep the plates at 4°C for about 1 week as a backup.
Inoculum in a shaker incubator for 6 h at 37°C.
Take 500 μL of inoculum and prepare glycerol stock by adding 500 μL of 50% glycerol, store immediately at −80°C.
Centrifuge the remaining inoculum at 2700 g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and add 500 μL of sterile water.
Centrifuge again, discard the supernatant, and add 500 μL of sterile water.
Mix well and store at 4°C. Use this as a template for colony PCR.
Set up the reaction in a thermocycler using primers mentioned in the key resources table.
Run 5 μL of the PCR product on a 1% agarose gel.
Proceed with Sanger sequencing using one positive colony from each gRNA group.
Use 15 μL of remaining PCR product for sequencing after the gel run.
Analyze Sanger sequencing data to confirm correct cloning of the gRNA sequence.
Compare sequencing data obtained with the gRNA sequence exactly.
If any clone yields a negative result, proceed to sequencing for subsequent clones.
Prepare 10 mL of LB broth (with ampicillin) for each gRNA.
Transfer a small volume of glycerol stock from positive clones into the LB broth using a sterile loop.
Inoculate the LB broth and incubate in a shaker incubator at 37°C for 16 h.
Isolate the plasmid using MN mini plasmid kit.
Dilute the isolated plasmids to achieve a final concentration of 500 ng/μL.
Store the plasmid at −20°C until use.
Seed healthy and actively dividing HEK293T cells in one well of 6 well plate so that it would reach 70–80% confluency in 24 h.
Ensure that HEK293T cells are approximately 80% confluent and healthy for transfection.
Bring the transfection reagent (FuGENE HD) to 25–30°C.
Prepare the transfection mixture as given below.
Incubate the mixture in 25–30°C for 15–20 min.
Remove the cell culture dish with HEK293T cells from the incubator.
Place the dish inside the biosafety cabinet.
Add the transfection reagent dropwise to the cells.
Gently swirl the dish to ensure even distribution of the mixture.
Return the dishes and incubate for 48 h.
Confirm successful transfection by using fluorescence microscopy on day 4.
Collect the supernatant from each well separately without disturbing the cells.
Clarify the supernatant by spinning at 400 g for 5 min at 25–30°C.
Transfer 2 mL of clarified supernatant to a tube containing 700 μL of virus concentrator.
Mix well and incubate at 4°C for 1 h.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2700 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of cold 1× PBS.
Store the sample immediately at -80°C and do not thaw until use.
Inoculate the bacterial stock in LB broth containing Ampicillin (100 μg/mL) and culture for 16 h.
Centrifuge the inoculum at 2700 g for 10 min at 25-30°C in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Collect the pellet for plasmid isolation, discarding the supernatant.
Isolate the plasmid using NucleoBond Xtra Midi EF kit.
Ensure the final concentration of plasmid preparation is not below 500 ng/μL.
Seed low passage HEK293T cells in a 10 cm cell culture dish to achieve 70-80% confluence in 24 h.
Make sure HEK293T cells are ∼80% confluent and healthy before transfection.
Bring the transfection reagent (FuGENE HD) to 25-30°C.
Vortex well and incubate at 25-30°C for 15 min after preparing the transfection mixture.
Gently add the transfection reagent mixture dropwise to the cell culture medium inside the Bio Safety Cabinet (BSC).
Swirl the dish to spread the mixture evenly and return the dishes to the incubator.
Collect the supernatant without disturbing the cells in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes to clarify the supernatant.
Transfer the clarified supernatant to a falcon tube containing 4× Lenti X concentrator or 4× PEG viral concentrator with a ratio of 1:3.
Mix well and incubate at 4°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2700 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the viral pellet in 200 μL of 1x PBS.
Make two aliquots of 100 μL each.
Store the virus at -80°C for downstream processes.
Seed 0.5 million cells per well in 2 wells of a 6 well plate.
Add 20 μL of 1 M HEPES buffer to each well.
Add 2 μL of polybrene (6 mg/mL) to each well.
Thaw the stored virus and add it into one well for transduction.
Spinfect the plate by centrifugation at 800 g for 30 min with low acceleration and brake settings (5 and 5).
Seal the plate with parafilm during centrifugation.
Return the plates to the incubator after centrifugation.
On day 12 & 14, check the viability of transduced cells.
Reseed viable transduced cells in a fresh 6 well plate.
Add 2 μL puromycin per mL of media (1 mg/mL) for both controls and transduced samples.
Check cells under a microscope after two days to assess cell death.
Perform a media change and reseed viable cells with the same concentration of puromycin.
Maintain stable cells from day 16–26 by continuing expansion.
Revive and expand the cryopreserved base editor stable cells by culturing them in growth medium supplemented with puromycin prior.
Maintain optimal cell density on alternate days, ensuring cells remain healthy and expand sufficiently.
After 10 days of puromycin selection, freeze cells in multiple vials as backup and store them in liquid nitrogen at -196°C.
Distribute 0.2 million cells per well in a 12-well plate using 1 mL of media for each well.
Add 10 μL of 1 M HEPES buffer and 1 μL of polybrene (6 mg/mL) to each well.
Thaw the stored lentivirus collected at 48 h and add it individually to each well.
Mix gently.
Centrifuge at 800 g for 30 min with minimum acceleration and brake.
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 48 hours.
Utilize approximately 150 μL of the cell culture for analysis.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS prior to analysis.
Evaluate transduction efficiency using flow cytometry by measuring the percentage of GFP expression.
Include a control group consisting of un-transduced cells for comparison.
Transfer the cells to fresh media in a 6 well plate if all cells are efficiently transduced with respective gRNA.
Perform media change by centrifuging the culture at 200 g and resuspending the cell pellet in fresh media on Day 4.
Cryopreserve adequate cells in appropriate freezing media for backup storage prior to media change.
Perform media change every 2 days from Day 6 to maintain healthy cells.
Discard any excess cells during maintenance.
Isolate DNA from 0.5 million cells using NucleoSpin Blood – DNA kit as per the manufacturer’s protocol.
Amplify the target region and perform Sanger sequencing/ targeted NGS using the primer mentioned in the key resources table.
Evaluate base editing efficiency using EditR software (Sanger sequencing data).
Evaluate base editing efficiency using CRISPResso2 software (NGS reads).
